This is pointing at no game in particular as the issue of daily quests is rampant in pretty much most of the MMO genre.

I do think always having something to do regularly is necessary, otherwise I would just only play my main character whenever there's a weekly lockout or a major raid to do or something, and spend the rest of my time leveling alts until I have one character for every day of the week. But the idea of a daily quest is sort of well, relentless. I know you're not "forced" to do them -- I can choose to ignore most of them, but then I feel like I'm being incredibly lazy (I mean, playing a game instead of doing something productive is already lazy in the first place, so now I'm being double-lazy) and not progressing as quickly as I should.

I think bi-daily quests would feel a lot less like a pain in the ass and less like they're consuming such huge chunks of gameplay time, as opposed to daily quests. A 48-hour time constraint just seems much easier to work with.

An alternative solution would be to do away with the concept entirely, and rather have max level progression work the same way leveling progression does -- more work produces more results, linearly. I don't have any ideas personally as to how this would work, but I'm sure there's already a game I don't know about that does it. The drawback of this is no-lifers pulling ahead of everyone else no matter what, but it solves the problems that daily quests have which are 1: Making you feel like there's a very specific quota to meet and 2: Making any gameplay on the same character after that quota feel pointless/redundant -- you're now out of daily quests to supplement your rewards, so you're basically just gold farming now.

Thoughts?
Should MMOs have bi-daily instead of daily quests?

In short, no. You said it yourself, you don't have to complete the dailies. If you're feeling overwhelmed by them, step back from the game just a bit to the point where you're enjoying yourself again.

They're not a means to artificially slow progress at all. They're a means to provide players with some direction in their daily activities. They're a means to provide a sense of progress where otherwise there would be none if you have already completely all of the one-time quests.

But the repetition does get tiresome after a while. I think it would at least be better if it's not the same crap every day and instead you got 4 or 5 random quests to do. From a large pool of possible quests to do -- if it's not big enough, then you still end up doing the same things 3 ~ 5 times before the week is over, assuming you're masochistic enough to bother.
If the repetition has grown tiresome, stop repeating. You can make that choice. You don't need the devs to make it for you.

I don't agree. You can provide direction without them. A sense of progress can be had without such basic repetition. If they daily quests do not provide some kind of incentive, nobody does them. If the incentive is a one-shot deal, people stop as soon as the incentive is reached.

That would add a lot of replay value for me.
MMOs should have no repeatable quests at all.
This kind of quests are supposed to be addictive and they are supposed to make players feel like they must keep pushing the button every day. It's by design, make no mistake.
